title: What if you could fly on Saturn's moon Titan? 🪐
subject: titan
description:
Would you strap on the wings? 👇

Saturn's largest moon, Titan, has 14% of Earth's gravity and surface air pressure about 1.5 times ours, which is why The Planetary Society calls it the easiest place in the Solar System to fly: a person could strap wings onto a suit and take off with a running start. You'd still need oxygen and heavy insulation at about -179°C (-290°F). The Huygens probe landed there on January 14, 2005, and NASA's Dragonfly rotorcraft is scheduled to launch in 2028.

Sources: The Planetary Society, "What would it be like to stand on the surface of Titan?" (Kate Howells, 2024); NASA Science, "Titan" and "Dragonfly" mission pages; ESA, "Huygens: science highlights" (2005).

scenes.text: On Titan, you could fly with wings on your arms.
Saturn's biggest moon has 14 percent of Earth's gravity and thicker air than ours.
Kate Howells of The Planetary Society calls it the easiest place in the Solar System to fly.
Skip the pressure suit. Bring oxygen and insulation: it's minus 290 Fahrenheit.
In 2005, the Huygens probe landed there and sent 72 minutes of data from the surface.
NASA's Dragonfly drone launches in 2028 to fly there first.
